etymology: From the webcomic: a sea lion follows you home, politely demanding that you justify yourself, forever.
committed_when: Someone has made a point and stopped engaging.
tell: A polite question arrives, then another, each one requiring homework, none of them answering anything.
counter: Name the pattern, not the message: state that the questions are endless and invite one. Answering the tenth is what keeps it going.
senses: Demanding endless evidence and civility from an opponent while offering none, so the exchange becomes the punishment.
It works because every single request is reasonable. Only the sequence is the tactic, and a sequence is invisible in any one message - which is why it is so hard to call out without looking rude.
example: *"I am just asking for a source. And for the methodology. And for the raw data. And for your credentials."* Four polite requests, one derailed argument.

confused_with.tell: The shift hands over the burden once; sealioning hands it over indefinitely, one request at a time.
